Scene: drawn directly into the world before fog, water, haze and glass, so they cover the ink like they would any other surface -- it is exposed physically rather than exposure-compensated (black ink stays black; coloured ink brightens or darkens with the scene like real pigment), and it also shows up in screen-space reflections (glossy floors/water reflect it) and is counted by auto-exposure metering. Camera (default): drawn before Night Mask, Graduated ND/Polarizer and bloom, so those and the glow apply to the ink too, like a captured element. Over atmosphere: drawn after fog and light shafts for a crisp line, still ahead of tonemapping and bloom composite. Overlay: flat, display-referred lines drawn after tonemapping, with no bloom or colour grade -- not available with the S-Log3 capture tonemapper (falls back to Camera). ev brightness volumetric halation color tint gel hue vcam lens lamp fixture look lut preset lightbox Lightbox rotoink_settings Roto Ink external external lightbox Lightbox External rotoink_settings rotoink_settings Roto Ink ri_sil_enable Silhouette check_box CineOutlineSilhouetteEnabled 3 e check_box Draw the outer silhouette line (a depth discontinuity between the subject and whatever is behind it). actor avatar cast lightbox Lightbox rotoink_settings Roto Ink external external lightbox Lightbox External rotoink_settings rotoink_settings Roto Ink ri_sil_thr_slider Silhouette threshold slider CineOutlineSilhouetteThreshold 3 e slider How big a relative depth step counts as a silhouette. Every frame: full quality, highest cost. Balanced: 2 faces per frame (~1/3 cost). Economy: 1 face per frame (~1/6 cost); both lag and can seam with flickering lights.
